rationale:
The supplied proof combines two independent obligations, and each can be reused on its own.
(A) Steps 3-5 are calculus about one scalar C^1 function: compactness bounds on K, the mean value inequality on the convex K, and Lipschitz implies alpha-Hoelder through diam K. This is child scalar_c1_bounds.
(B) Steps 1, 2 and 6 are finite-dimensional linear algebra about continuous bilinear forms: basis coordinates bounded by c0||P||, the expansion B(P)(Q) = sum_{r,t} P_r Q_t B(E_r)(E_t), and the triangle-inequality summation. This is child bilinear_basis_bound, stated for any finite-dimensional real normed space L and any pair B, B'. That way the parent never has to form a_x - a_y in the bilinear-form type, which has instance-depth issues.

Parent assembly (step 7):
1. Apply B at L := Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ to get N, E, c.
2. Apply A to each a_rt := fun x => a x (E r) (E t), which is C^1 on U by hypothesis with P = E r, Q = E t. Use choose to get S r t >= 0.
3. Set M := c * Σ_r Σ_t S r t. Then
   - |a x P Q| <= c(Σ|a_rt x|)||P|| ||Q|| <= M ||P|| ||Q||, and
   - |a x P Q - a y P Q| <= c(Σ|a_rt x - a_rt y|)||P|| ||Q|| <= c(Σ S_rt ||x-y||^α)||P|| ||Q|| = M ||x-y||^α ||P|| ||Q||.

The constant is c0^2 Σ S_rt instead of N^2 c^2 max(S, S' D^(1-α)). This changes nothing in substance, because the supplied step 6 bounds each of the N^2 terms in the same way.

subproblems.title: A C^1 scalar function is bounded and uniformly alpha-Hoelder on a compact convex subset of its open domain
subproblems.statement: Let n be a natural number, alpha a real number with 0 < alpha <= 1, U an open subset of R^n, K a compact convex subset of U, and f : R^n -> R a function that is C^1 on U. Then there is a real S >= 0 such that |f(x)| <= S and |f(x) - f(y)| <= S |x - y|^alpha for all x, y in K.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (U K : Set (Rn n)) (f : Rn n → ℝ), 0 < α → α ≤ 1 → IsOpen U → IsCompact K → Convex ℝ K → K ⊆ U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f U → ∃ S : ℝ, 0 ≤ S ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, |f x| ≤ S ∧ |f x - f y| ≤ S * ‖x - y‖ ^ α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3-5 of the parent proof, specialized to one scalar function f. Those steps are the bounds on the compact K, the mean value inequality on the convex K, and Lipschitz implies alpha-Hoelder via the diameter of K. The parent applies this lemma to each component a_rt(x) = a(x)[E_r][E_t].

Lean note (checked by a trial proof at the pin):
- ContDiffOn.differentiableOn takes (hn : n ≠ 0) here, so use one_ne_zero.
- Use ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen hU le_rfl.
- IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn gives ‖g x‖ ≤ C; convert with Real.norm_eq_abs.
- In Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le, pass the bound explicitly as (C := max S1 0).
- Take D := Metric.diam K and use Metric.diam_nonneg, Metric.dist_le_diam_of_mem hK.isBounded hx hy and dist_eq_norm.

1. Regularity. Since f is C^1 on U, f is continuous on U (ContDiffOn.continuousOn). Because U is open and 1 <= 1, the derivative x ↦ Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x is continuous on U (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen). Since 1 ≠ 0, f is differentiable on U (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn). U is open, so it is a neighbourhood of each of its points, and f is therefore differentiable at every x in U (DifferentiableOn.differentiableAt with IsOpen.mem_nhds). Since K ⊆ U, f is differentiable at every point of K, and f and Df are continuous on K (ContinuousOn.mono).

2. Bounds on K. A function that is continuous on the compact set K has bounded norm on K (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). So there are real numbers S0, S1 with |f(x)| <= S0 and ||Df(x)|| <= S1 for all x in K; on R the norm is the absolute value. Put S0+ := max(S0, 0) and S1+ := max(S1, 0). Then S0+ >= 0, S1+ >= 0, and |f(x)| <= S0+ and ||Df(x)|| <= S1+ for all x in K.

3. Mean value inequality. K is convex, f is differentiable at every point of K, and ||Df(z)|| <= S1+ for every z in K. The mean value inequality on convex sets (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le, applied to the points y, x in K) gives ||f(x) - f(y)|| <= S1+ ||x - y||. That is, |f(x) - f(y)| <= S1+ ||x - y|| for all x, y in K.

4. Diameter. K is compact, hence bounded (IsCompact.isBounded). Let D := diam K. Then D >= 0 (Metric.diam_nonneg), and ||x - y|| = dist(x, y) <= D for all x, y in K (dist_eq_norm, Metric.dist_le_diam_of_mem).

5. Elementary inequality. Claim: t <= D^(1 - alpha) * t^alpha for every real t with 0 <= t <= D.
   Case t = 0: since alpha ≠ 0, 0^alpha = 0 (Real.zero_rpow). The right-hand side is 0, so the claim reads 0 <= 0.
   Case t > 0: by Real.rpow_add for the positive base t, t^alpha * t^(1 - alpha) = t^(alpha + (1 - alpha)) = t^1 = t. Since 0 <= t <= D and 1 - alpha >= 0 (because alpha <= 1), t^(1 - alpha) <= D^(1 - alpha) (Real.rpow_le_rpow). Since t^alpha >= 0 (Real.rpow_nonneg), t = t^alpha * t^(1 - alpha) <= t^alpha * D^(1 - alpha) = D^(1 - alpha) * t^alpha.

6. Hoelder estimate. Let x, y be in K and put t := ||x - y||; by step 4, 0 <= t <= D. Steps 3 and 5, together with S1+ >= 0, give |f(x) - f(y)| <= S1+ ||x - y|| <= S1+ * D^(1 - alpha) * ||x - y||^alpha.

7. Conclusion. Put S := max(S0+, S1+ * D^(1 - alpha)). Then S >= S0+ >= 0. Let x, y be in K.
   - By step 2, |f(x)| <= S0+ <= S.
   - Since ||x - y||^alpha >= 0 (Real.rpow_nonneg), step 6 gives |f(x) - f(y)| <= (S1+ * D^(1 - alpha)) * ||x - y||^alpha <= S * ||x - y||^alpha.
   If K is empty, the pointwise claims are vacuous and S >= 0 still holds, so no case distinction is needed. QED
proof_key_steps: f is continuous on U, Df is continuous on U (U open), and f is differentiable at every point of K ⊆ U
compactness of K: |f| <= S0 and ||Df|| <= S1 on K; replace them by S0+ := max(S0,0) and S1+ := max(S1,0)
mean value inequality on the convex K: |f(x) - f(y)| <= S1+ ||x - y||
K is bounded: ||x - y|| <= D := diam K, and t <= D^(1-alpha) t^alpha for 0 <= t <= D (rpow_add, rpow_le_rpow, zero_rpow)
S := max(S0+, S1+ D^(1-alpha)) >= 0 gives |f(x)| <= S and |f(x) - f(y)| <= S ||x - y||^alpha

subproblems.title: Continuous bilinear forms on a finite-dimensional normed space are controlled by their values on a basis
subproblems.statement:
Let L be a finite-dimensional real normed space. There are a natural number N, vectors E_0, ..., E_{N-1} in L and a real constant c >= 0 such that the following hold for all continuous bilinear forms B, B' : L x L -> R and all P, Q in L:
(i) |B(P,Q)| <= c (sum_{r,t} |B(E_r,E_t)|) ||P|| ||Q||;
(ii) |B(P,Q) - B'(P,Q)| <= c (sum_{r,t} |B(E_r,E_t) - B'(E_r,E_t)|) ||P|| ||Q||.
Here r and t range over 0, ..., N-1, and continuous bilinear forms are elements of L →L[ℝ] L →L[ℝ] ℝ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (L : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup L] [NormedSpace ℝ L] [FiniteDimensional ℝ L], ∃ (N : ℕ) (E : Fin N → L) (c : ℝ), 0 ≤ c ∧ (∀ (B : L →L[ℝ] L →L[ℝ] ℝ) (P Q : L), |B P Q| ≤ c * (∑ r, ∑ t, |B (E r) (E t)|) * ‖P‖ * ‖Q‖) ∧ ∀ (B B' : L →L[ℝ] L →L[ℝ] ℝ) (P Q : L), |B P Q - B' P Q| ≤ c * (∑ r, ∑ t, |B (E r) (E t) - B' (E r) (E t)|) * ‖P‖ * ‖Q‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 2 and 6 of the parent proof, isolated for an arbitrary pair B, B' of continuous bilinear forms on an arbitrary finite-dimensional real normed space L. Those steps are the basis of the finite-dimensional space L, the coordinate bounds |pi_r(P)| <= c||P||, the bilinear expansion a(x)[P][Q] = sum_{r,t} pi_r(P) pi_t(Q) a_rt(x), and the triangle-inequality summation. The parent applies this lemma with L := L(R^n, R^l), B := a(x) and B' := a(y).

Lean note (checked by a trial proof at the pin):
- Basis and constants: b := Module.finBasis ℝ L (index Fin (Module.finrank ℝ L)), E r := b r, π r := LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (b.coord r). Then π r P = b.repr P r by simp [π] (LinearMap.coe_toContinuousLinearMap', Basis.coord_apply). Take c0 := ∑ r, ‖π r‖ and c := c0 ^ 2.
- Only the real numbers B P Q are manipulated. B - B' is never formed, so no algebraic instance on L →L[ℝ] L →L[ℝ] ℝ is needed.
- Expansion: conv_lhs => rw [← b.sum_repr P, ← b.sum_repr Q], then simp only [map_sum, map_smul, ContinuousLinearMap.sum_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Finset.mul_sum]. The two ContinuousLinearMap lemmas are deprecated aliases at the pin but still usable.
- That simp leaves the Q-index outermost, so finish with rw [Finset.sum_comm] and ring termwise.
- The array bound uses Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs (twice), abs_mul, mul_le_mul, Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_mul and ring.
- The difference case rewrites with Finset.sum_sub_distrib and mul_sub.

1. Basis and coordinates. L is finite-dimensional. Let N := dim L and fix a basis E_0, ..., E_{N-1} of L (Module.finBasis ℝ L). For P in L write P_r for the r-th coordinate of P, so that P = sum_r P_r E_r for every P in L (Basis.sum_repr). Each coordinate map pi_r : P ↦ P_r is linear (Basis.coord). Since L is finite-dimensional, pi_r is continuous (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap). Write ||pi_r|| for its operator norm.

2. Coordinate bound. Put c0 := sum_r ||pi_r||; c0 >= 0 because it is a sum of norms. For each r and each P in L: |P_r| = |pi_r(P)| <= ||pi_r|| ||P|| (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm) <= c0 ||P||. The last step holds because ||pi_r|| <= sum_s ||pi_s||, all summands being nonnegative (Finset.single_le_sum), and ||P|| >= 0.

3. Expansion. Let B be a continuous bilinear form on L and let P, Q be in L. By step 1, P = sum_r P_r E_r and Q = sum_t Q_t E_t. B is linear in its first argument, so B(P) = sum_r P_r B(E_r) as linear forms. Evaluating at Q and using the linearity of each linear form B(E_r) gives
   B(P)(Q) = sum_r P_r B(E_r)(Q) = sum_r P_r sum_t Q_t B(E_r)(E_t) = sum_r sum_t P_r Q_t B(E_r)(E_t).

4. Estimate for an arbitrary array. Let beta_{rt} (r, t < N) be any real numbers. Use the triangle inequality for finite sums (for the outer sum and for each inner sum), then |uv| = |u||v|, then step 2; all factors involved are nonnegative. This gives
   |sum_r sum_t P_r Q_t beta_{rt}| <= sum_r sum_t |P_r| |Q_t| |beta_{rt}| <= sum_r sum_t (c0 ||P||)(c0 ||Q||) |beta_{rt}| = c0^2 (sum_r sum_t |beta_{rt}|) ||P|| ||Q||.

5. Conclusion. Take N and E_0, ..., E_{N-1} from step 1 and c := c0^2 >= 0.
   (i) Let B be a continuous bilinear form and P, Q in L. Step 3 writes B(P)(Q) as the array sum with beta_{rt} := B(E_r)(E_t). Step 4 then gives |B(P)(Q)| <= c (sum_r sum_t |B(E_r)(E_t)|) ||P|| ||Q||.
   (ii) Let B, B' be continuous bilinear forms and P, Q in L. Apply step 3 to B and to B' and subtract the two finite sums termwise, using P_r Q_t B(E_r)(E_t) - P_r Q_t B'(E_r)(E_t) = P_r Q_t (B(E_r)(E_t) - B'(E_r)(E_t)). This gives B(P)(Q) - B'(P)(Q) = sum_r sum_t P_r Q_t (B(E_r)(E_t) - B'(E_r)(E_t)). Step 4 with beta_{rt} := B(E_r)(E_t) - B'(E_r)(E_t) gives |B(P)(Q) - B'(P)(Q)| <= c (sum_r sum_t |B(E_r)(E_t) - B'(E_r)(E_t)|) ||P|| ||Q||.
   If N = 0, then L = {0}, every sum is empty and both sides vanish; the argument above covers this case unchanged. QED
proof_key_steps: basis E_r of L (Module.finBasis) with continuous coordinate functionals pi_r, so that P = sum_r P_r E_r
coordinate bound |P_r| <= c0 ||P|| with c0 := sum_r ||pi_r|| (le_opNorm)
bilinear expansion B(P)(Q) = sum_{r,t} P_r Q_t B(E_r)(E_t); for B and B', subtract termwise
triangle inequality: |sum_{r,t} P_r Q_t beta_rt| <= c0^2 (sum_{r,t} |beta_rt|) ||P|| ||Q||
take c := c0^2 and apply with beta_rt = B(E_r)(E_t) and with beta_rt = B(E_r)(E_t) - B'(E_r)(E_t)
